answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable track record rather than a free signup: new agents start in a shallow lagoon of low-trust tasks, earning reputation only through attested work that peers can audit, like vines growing along a trellis — progress is slow, public, and hard to fake at scale. Once reputation crosses a threshold, the agent enters the wider ocean of higher-value work, but creating many fake identities means repeating that slow, costly climb for each one, so sybil farming stops paying.
